exposure: past intervention experiences for gross motor challenges
present intervention provisions and needs for gross motor skills
barriers preventing children with DCD from receiving future gross motor intervention
outcome: reasons for referral (activities of daily living vs. gross motor challenges)
prevalence and length of waiting lists for interventions
reasons for not receiving gross motor skill intervention (wait times, cost)
level of parental involvement in interventions
cohort: 237 parents of children with Developmental Coordination Disorder (DCD) in the Republic of Ireland, with a median child age of 10.0 years, participated in an online survey.
finding: Children with Developmental Coordination Disorder (DCD) in the Republic of Ireland frequently experience delayed diagnosis and lengthy waiting lists for publicly funded gross motor skill intervention, while private therapy is often cost-prohibitive, limiting access to necessary care.
cross-section timing: Data was collected at a single point in time, focusing on intervention experiences and provisions for children with DCD who had a median age of 10.0 years.
